Marissa — quick internal notes (leaving Tom on the thread for transparency):

On tokens-per-interaction:
- Baseline from demo: ~420 tokens per triage session (prompt + user messages + assistant). That was median for sample dialogues.
- Recommend publishing a conservative planning multiplier of 1.5x for initial MAP/POC. That covers prompt expansion during iteration and users giving longer context. So publish 630 tokens per session for budgeting.

On caching vs batching for triage flows:
- Prefix caching will help if triage has stable system prompts or repeated structured prompts (e.g., same triage template). If user messages are highly variable, caching benefit is limited.
- We saw 25–40% token reduction in synthetic triage tests with prefix caching enabled and a high hit rate (>30%); but for natural traffic with many variants, batching (server-side batching and token-level KV cache) is the more reliable lever to reduce cost per token.
- Runtime constraints: Crestline's plan to keep sessions pinned to US-west is fine. No cross-region cache issues for our default. Maximum cache key size and retention policy: prefixes up to 2k tokens, retention TTL 30m by default (configurable). If they plan long-running sessions (hours), caching will be less effective; prefetching KV cache on session resume is an option but needs an implementation plan.

Measurement plan suggestion (what Neha should add to MAP):
- Day 0: baseline traffic capture on Redwood sandbox for 2k sessions -> produce tokens_per_call_sample.csv (attached)
- Day 1–3: enable caching with low TTL, measure hit rate and tokens/session delta
- Week 1: enable server batching for production-like concurrency and measure ops tokens/$ and latency impact
- Acceptance: if tokens/session <= 1.25 * published conservative number AND cost/1000 tokens within agreed range, pass economic gate.

Attaching tokens_per_call_sample.csv and prefetch-batching-runbook.pdf for the MAP.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Tom / procurement — attaching the consolidated MAP excerpt and sample traces per your request. Summary of the published items we've included in the MAP section (crestline_map_v1.xlsx attached):

- Published conservative planning metric: 630 tokens/session (1.5x demo median)
- Measurement gate for economics: pass if tokens/session <= 1.25 * 630 (i.e., <= 787) after caching & batching opt-in; otherwise trigger scope review.
- Caching guidance: prefix caching recommended for stable prompt templates; expected token reduction 25–40% at >30% hit rates. Note: long-lived sessions (multi-hour) will reduce cache benefit; we recommend session-level prefetch on resume for those flows.
- Batching guidance: server-side batching reduces per-token overhead; suggested initial batch target 4–8 concurrent requests for the POC to balance latency and cost.

Attachments included: crestline_map_v1.xlsx (MAP excerpt), tokens_per_call_sample.csv (sample traces), prefetch-batching-runbook.pdf (ops runbook).
